title: Measuring transferable wind-power dynamics with explicit event protocols

abstract: Wind-power event catalogues connect production variability to forecasting and flexibility decisions. We introduce a protocol-aware evaluation framework that separates interval support, retained trajectory information and decision value. The framework links seven wind-farm archives containing 333 turbines through explicit detection, matching and representation contracts. The five-farm primary benchmark provides 1.54 million complete shapes and 1.47 million matched comparisons. Ordered trajectories yield cross-detector normalized mutual information of 0.590–0.698, compared with 0.024–0.067 after correspondence permutation. Signed and temporal encoders preserve strong grouping information, and external Greek and SDWPF archives extend the evaluation. Fresh post-selection synthetic sequences give KAN-AD mean F1 0.793 versus 0.732 for a validation-selected mean-change rule; higher noise increases the advantage of learned scores. A policy-grounded 10%-power, two-hour storage benchmark exposes the conditions under which ramp-focused forecasts change operating cost. Conventional imbalance-price cases favor whole-period forecast accuracy; high penalties for severe deviations can favor event weighting in selected scenarios. We establish protocol-aware measurement as a reproducible layer for wind-power event science: every comparison carries its catalogue reach, information preservation and decision value. Open data, analysis code and a blinded multi-rater interface make this evaluation procedure reusable.
highlights: A protocol-aware framework links event support, representation and decision value.
Seven wind-farm archives provide explicit cross-detector event comparisons.
Frozen learned scores retain episode discrimination as synthetic noise rises.
A 10%-power, two-hour storage benchmark exposes forecast decision conditions.
A blinded multi-rater interface supports independent event-region annotation.
